issue_2_os_worker_process_deadline_termi.prior_bug_in_51e6ec4d: In commit 51e6ec4d, run_bounded_256_context_winner_generation() used ThreadPoolExecutor with ex.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True). In Python, shutdown(wait=False) does not stop running threads, and Python's threading._shutdown waits for non-daemon ThreadPoolExecutor threads at interpreter exit; furthermore, a single blocked rollout call in run_matched_v3_acceptance_test() was only checked between contexts.
issue_2_os_worker_process_deadline_termi.fix_implemented: Replaced ThreadPoolExecutor in verify_flywheel_wider_train_extension_v3.py with DeadlineController.run_batch_in_killable_workers(), which spawns forked OS worker processes (multiprocessing.get_context('fork').Process) placed in dedicated process groups (os.setpgrp()). Upon deadline expiry, _terminate_active() immediately sends SIGKILL to the worker process group (os.killpg(pid, signal.SIGKILL)) and worker PID (os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)) and reaps the child (proc.join), guaranteeing zero surviving background workers, zero late file writes after deadline, and immediate Python interpreter exit. Also added DeadlineController.itimer_guard() (using kernel signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, ...)) around run_matched_v3_acceptance_test() so a blocked in-process rollout call is preempted at the hard deadline.
